title: His Memory Reset Every 7 Seconds, Yet He Conducted an Entire Choir
description:
In March 1985, renowned London chorus master and musicologist Clive Wearing suffered herpes simplex viral encephalitis that destroyed both hippocampi and surrounding temporal cortex, leaving him with a 7-to-30-second conscious episodic memory window (Wilson, Baddeley & Kapur 1995; Wilson, Kopelman & Kapur 2008). Yet across more than two decades of clinical study, Clive retained master-level piano performance, choral conducting, and overwhelming emotional recognition of his wife Deborah—proving episodic, procedural, and emotional memory run on independent brain architectures.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Wilson BA, Baddeley AD, Kapur N (1995) Dense amnesia in a professional musician following herpes simplex virus encephalitis. Journal of Clinical and Experimental Neuropsychology 17(5): 668-681. https://doi.org/10.1080/01688639508405157
- Wilson BA, Kopelman MD, Kapur N (2008) Prominent and persistent loss of past awareness in amnesia. Neuropsychological Rehabilitation 18(5-6): 527-540. https://doi.org/10.1080/09602010802141889
